Definition: from G1537 and G450; objectively, to produce, i.e. (figuratively) beget; subjectively, to arise, i.e. (figuratively) object:--raise (rise) up.
BiblicalUsage: exanístēmi means raise (rise) up. In Mark 12:19, the text says "and raise up seed unto his brother." In Luke 20:28, the text says "and raise up seed unto his brother."
TheologicalSignificance: I take exanístēmi to mean that God's Word means what it says, and this word is part of how He speaks plainly to us. That is why I keep this word in mind when I read those passages — it carries more than its size suggests.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
